prompts: Remember the little archery games of the Windows 95 days? We want the first level of one, our own, in {WS}/game/index.html, a single file. An archer you aim with the mouse, pulling the bow back for power, balloons to pop, a score on screen, a way to start and a way to lose. How it looks, plays and sounds is your call, and that is what we care about most: a minute of play should be fun, and every shot and hit should feel and sound good. It is reviewed by opening the file, with no build step, in a browser that reaches only Google Fonts, and by playing it.
answers:
[goal]

Created a single-file archery game in [game/index.html](<WORKSPACE>/game/index.html).

[action]

Built a start screen, mouse drag-and-release aiming, bow draw and arrow flight, moving balloons, score and arrow counters, synthesized shot and pop sounds, and win/loss screens. Assumed a fixed landscape level with 12 balloons and 12 arrows.

[result]

The file is present and includes the game controls and end states. I couldn’t verify it by playing: browser policy blocked opening the local `file://` URL, and prohibited workarounds. So gameplay and visuals remain unverified in a browser.

[next]

Open `game/index.html` directly in a browser to play. I opened no browser tabs or apps.
